purpose: Extract reusable single-character writing knowledge from transmitted Wang-form vocabulary without treating Huairen's assembled adjacency as Wang Xizhi flow evidence.

authority.studySupport: Palace Museum technical study explicitly treats dot/stroke methods, component combination, structural features, difficult/near-form characters and same-character variants as study dimensions.

stableSkeleton.definition: Features that should survive across legitimate variants of the same character.

variableZones.definition: Places where Wang-form vocabulary permits controlled change without losing character identity.
observe: stroke joining versus separation inside one glyph
square versus rounded turning in transmitted form

transmissionNoise.definition: Features not promoted to Wang Xizhi brush grammar without corroborating ink evidence.
exclude: micro-pressure claims inferred only from black/white width
inter-character spacing in Huairen's assembled inscription

extract: 知/日-like component relationship as transmitted
which internal strokes may simplify or join
candidate component analogues elsewhere in Wang-form corpus
慧.confidenceRule: One occurrence cannot define a Wang invariant by itself. Promote observations as hypotheses until corroborated by other Wang-form or ink witnesses.

comparisonProtocol: Retrieve only the needed remote glyph regions through the existing resource/transcode layer; never download the whole work by default.
Normalize comparison scale for structural inspection, but retain original aspect ratio metadata.
Trace component topology before tracing stroke contour.
Mark each observed feature as invariant-candidate, variable-zone, or transmission-uncertain.
Require at least two independent occurrences or corroborating Wang evidence before promoting a feature to stableSkeleton.
Never use neighboring inscription characters to infer entry, exit, spacing or qi-flow.

allowed: select among historically supported single-glyph structures
learn how far a component may compress, displace or simplify
construct missing-character hypotheses from Wang component grammar only after provenance labeling
counter-check whether a reconstructed glyph looks font-like or mechanically regular
blocked: derive ligature decisions between target scripture characters
claim a reconstructed form is an attested Wang Xizhi glyph

flowEvidenceSeparation.singleGlyphTeacher: 聖教序 may teach how a character can be built.
flowEvidenceSeparation.flowTeacher: Flow must come from continuous-writing witnesses such as credible manuscript/copy passages preserving sequential relationships.
flowEvidenceSeparation.mergeRule: Project Hand may later place a Shengjiao-informed glyph into a phrase only after Flow Engine independently determines scale, lean, spacing, entry/exit adaptation and phrase rhythm.

nextGate.name: remote-glyph-region-comparison
nextGate.requirement: Bind remote regions for repeated 是、智、端 and the single 慧, then populate observed invariant-candidates and variable zones. Do not use inscription adjacency.
